findings.title: Device tagging now synchronous on every anonymous request
findings.body: TagDevice used to run in a background goroutine. It now runs inline with the request context. Each anonymous request that misses the local cache now waits on DB writes before authenticating. When a device limit is set, that includes an extra COUNT query. A slow or failing DB therefore adds latency to anonymous authentication. Request cancellation can also abort the tagging.

findings.title: Cache set before store write lets rejected devices bypass the limit
findings.body: tagDeviceUI writes the cache key before calling CreateOrUpdateDevice. If the store returns ErrDeviceLimitReached, the first request fails. Later requests from the same device hit the cache, get nil back, and authenticate successfully for the 29-minute cache TTL. The limit is effectively enforced only once per cache period.

findings.title: Race between count and insert lets the limit be exceeded
findings.body: CountDevices and the upsert run as separate statements with no transaction or lock. Concurrent new devices can all read a count below the limit and all insert. The number of stored devices can then exceed the configured limit.

findings.title: Zero rows affected misreported on MySQL
findings.body: On MySQL, RowsAffected counts only rows whose values actually changed. If an existing device is updated with identical values (same IP, user agent and second-precision timestamp), it returns 0. A legitimate existing device is then rejected with ErrDeviceLimitReached.
